anges%20the%20force.%20Nothing%20about%20the%20movement%20is%20dictated%20in%20advance.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20That%20feedback%20loop%20is%20what%20turns%20muscle%20simulation%20into%20*musculoskeletal*%20simulation.%20The%20muscle%20and%20the%20skeleton%20are%20now%20two%20dynamical%20systems%20wired%20into%20each%20other%2C%20and%20we%20have%20to%20integrate%20them%20together.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Read%20a%20short%20explanation%2C%20predict%20what%20the%20leg%20and%20the%20muscle%20should%20do%2C%20run%20the%20cell%2C%20and%20then%20use%20the%20plot%20to%20answer%20the%20challenge%20questions.%20Keep%20a%20scratchpad%20nearby%20and%20write%20your%20prediction%20*before*%20you%20reveal%20each%20plot.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20You%20do%20not%20need%20to%20finish%20every%20challenge%20on%20the%20first%20pass.%20Run%20the%20cells%20in%20order%20first%3B%20then%20come%20back%20and%20change%20one%20parameter%20at%20a%20time.%20The%20goal%20is%20not%20to%20make%20the%20code%20run%20%E2%80%94%20it%20already%20runs.%20The%20goal%20is%20to%20connect%20the%20free-body%20diagram%2C%20the%20coupled%20differential%20equations%2C%20and%20the%20movement%20you%20see%20in%20the%20plots.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%200.**%20Before%20you%20begin%2C%20picture%20the%20task%20we%20are%20about%20to%20simulate%3A%20a%20seated%20person%20with%20the%20knee%20flexed%20at%20%2490%5Eo%24%20suddenly%20activates%20the%20quadriceps%20fully%2C%20and%20the%20leg%20swings%20up%20into%20extension.%20Predict%20three%20things%20and%20write%20them%20down%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20As%20the%20knee%20extends%2C%20does%20the%20quadriceps%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20shorten%20or%20lengthen%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Gravity%20pulls%20the%20leg%20back%20down.%20Early%20in%20the%20movement%20(knee%20near%20%2490%5Eo%24)%2C%20does%20gravity%20help%20or%20oppose%20the%20extension%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20muscle%20shortens%20*while*%20producing%20force.%20From%20the%20force-velocity%20relationship%20you%20met%20in%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py)%2C%20should%20the%20force%20rise%20or%20fall%20as%20the%20shortening%20speeds%20up%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Connect%20the%20existing%20muscle%20model%20to%20a%20joint%20equation.%20Now%20joint%20angle%20affects%20musculotendon%20length%2C%20and%20muscle%20force%20affects%20joint%20acceleration.%20Track%20this%20feedback%20through%20the%20state%20vector%2C%20then%20compare%20the%20constant%20and%20measured%20moment%20arms%20without%20mixing%20their%20geometry.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Try%20the%20distributed%20**Exercises**%20before%20opening%20their%20collapsed%20worked%20solutions.%20Then%20use%20the%20**Checkpoint%20questions**%20and%20attempt%20the%20**Problems**%20independently%3B%20their%20panels%20contain%20final%20answers%20only.%20Predict%20the%20effect%20of%20a%20parameter%20change%20before%20running%20it%2C%20and%20check%20units%20and%20limiting%20cases.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Opening%20challenge.**%20A%20muscle%20pulls%20on%20a%20freely%20moving%20shank.%20Why%20can%20doubling%20its%20force%20fail%20to%20double%20the%20final%20knee%20angle%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Python%20setup%0A%0A%20%20%20%20The%20dependency%20declaration%20at%20the%20top%20of%20this%20file%20lists%20the%20packages%20used%20by%20this%20guide.%20Marimo%20runs%20cells%20in%20dependency%20order.%20Run%20the%20notebook%20in%20an%20editor%20to%20use%20its%20displays%20and%20controls%3B%20the%20computational%20examples%20below%20explain%20their%20inputs%20before%20using%20them.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20We%20will%20now%20simulate%20the%20dynamics%20of%20the%20musculoskeletal%20system%20with%20muscle%20dynamics.%20You%20should%20have%20read%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py)%20and%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%20first.%20In%20addition%2C%20chapter%204%20of%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%20(2006)%20is%20a%20good%20introduction%20to%20this%20topic.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Forward%20and%20inverse%20dynamics%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20a%20typical%20movement%20analysis%20using%20inverse%20dynamics%2C%20we%20would%20measure%20the%20leg%20and%20thigh%20positions%2C%20calculate%20the%20leg%20and%20knee%20linear%20and%20angular%20position%20and%20acceleration%2C%20and%20then%20estimate%20the%20net%20moment%20of%20force%20at%20the%20knee%20joint%20and%20the%20force%20of%20the%20quadriceps%20muscle.%20Now%20we%20want%20to%20do%20the%20opposite%3A%20perform%20*forward*%20dynamics%2C%20where%20muscle%20force%20is%20the%20input%20and%20the%20movement%20of%20the%20leg%20is%20the%20output.%20The%20figure%20below%20compares%20the%20two%20approaches.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2FInvDirDyn.png%22%20width%3D%22600%22%20alt%3D%22Forward%20and%20inverse%20dynamics.%22%20%2F%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Figure.%20Inverse%20dynamics%20and%20Forward%20(or%20Direct)%20dynamics%20approaches%20for%20movement%20analysis%20(adapted%20from%20Zajac%20and%20Gordon%2C%201989).*%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%201.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Inverse%20dynamics%20starts%20from%20measured%20movement%20and%20works%20backwards%20to%20forces.%20Forward%20dynamics%20starts%20from%20forces%20and%20works%20forwards%20to%20movement.%20Which%20one%20can%20predict%20a%20movement%20that%20has%20*never%20been%20measured*%2C%20and%20why%20does%20that%20matter%20for%20answering%20questions%20such%20as%20%22what%20would%20happen%20if%20this%20muscle%20were%20weaker%3F%22%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Inverse%20dynamics%20gives%20you%20the%20*net*%20joint%20moment.%20Why%20can%20it%20not%20tell%20you%2C%20on%20its%20own%2C%20how%20much%20of%20that%20moment%20came%20from%20the%20quadriceps%20and%20how%20much%20from%20a%20co-contracting%20hamstring%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Forward%20dynamics%20needs%20an%20initial%20state%20(position%20and%20velocity)%20and%20it%20needs%20to%20be%20integrated%20in%20time.%20Inverse%20dynamics%20needs%20neither.%20What%20does%20that%20tell%20you%20about%20which%20of%20the%20two%20accumulates%20numerical%20error%20over%20a%20long%20trial%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20**Exercise%201%20%E2%80%94%20Convert%20force%20to%20torque.**%20A%20tendon%20force%20of%20800%20N%20acts%20with%20a%200.04%20m%20knee%20moment%20arm.%20Find%20its%20torque.%20If%20the%20joint%20moves%20at%202%20rad%2Fs%2C%20what%20is%20its%20joint%20power%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Solution%20to%20Exercise%201'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Ctau%3DrF%3D32%24%20N%20m%20and%20%24P%3D%5Ctau%5Cdot%5Ctheta%3D64%24%20W%20for%20matching%20positive%20signs.%20The%20moment%20arm%20also%20controls%20the%20musculotendon%20length%20rate%2C%20so%20changing%20it%20alters%20both%20torque%20and%20fiber%20dynamics.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20One-link%20system%20with%20one%20DoF%20and%20one%20muscle%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20start%20with%20the%20simplest%20case%2C%20a%20one-link%20rigid%20body%20with%20one%20degree%20of%20freedom%20and%20one%20muscle.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20simulate%20the%20extension%20movement%20of%20the%20knee.%20This%20problem%20is%20based%20on%20an%20example%20from%20chapter%204%20of%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%20(2006).%20We%20will%20model%20the%20task%20as%20a%20planar%20movement%2C%20the%20leg%20and%20foot%20as%20one%20rigid%20segment%20and%20the%20rest%20of%20the%20body%20as%20fixed%2C%20the%20knee%20as%20a%20revolute%20joint%20with%20a%20fixed%20axis%20of%20rotation%20and%20one%20degree%20of%20freedom%2C%20and%20only%20one%20muscle%20as%20knee%20extensor%2C%20as%20illustrated%20in%20the%20figure%20below.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%3Cimg%20src%3D%22https%3A%2F%2Fraw.githubusercontent.com%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fmaster%2Fimages%2Fknee.png%22%20width%3D%22500%22%20alt%3D%22Planar%20knee%20model.%22%20%2F%3E%0A%0A%20%20%20%20*Figure.%20Planar%20model%20of%20the%20knee%20with%20one%20degree%20of%20freedom%2C%20one%20extensor%20muscle%2C%20and%20the%20corresponding%20free-body%20diagram%20for%20the%20leg.%20%24%5Ctheta%24%3A%20knee%20angle%20with%20the%20horizontal%3B%20%24F_M%24%3A%20force%20of%20the%20quadriceps%20muscle%3B%20%24F_J%24%3A%20force%20at%20the%20knee%20joint%3B%20%24r_M%24%3A%20moment%20arm%20of%20the%20quadriceps%3B%20%24r_%7Bcm%7D%24%3A%20distance%20from%20the%20knee%20joint%20to%20the%20center%20of%20mass%20of%20the%20leg%2Bfoot%20segment%3B%20%24mg%24%3A%20weight%20of%20the%20leg%2Bfoot%3B%20%24L_%7BMT0%7D%24%3A%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20length%20at%20%24%5Ctheta%20%3D%2090%5Eo%24.*%0A%0A%20%20%20%20From%20the%20figure%20above%2C%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equation%20for%20the%20sum%20of%20moments%20of%20force%20around%20the%20knee%20joint%20is%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24r_M%20F_M%20%2B%20r_%7Bcm%7D%5Ccos(%5Ctheta)mg%20%3D%20I%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%5E2%20%5Ctheta%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%5E2%7D%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20where%20%24I%24%20is%20the%20rotational%20inertia%20of%20the%20leg%2Bfoot%20segment%20around%20the%20knee%20joint.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20In%20our%20convention%2C%20the%20first%20term%20on%20the%20left-hand%20side%20is%20a%20positive%20(extensor)%20moment%20of%20force%2C%20and%20the%20second%20term%20becomes%20a%20negative%20(flexor)%20moment%20of%20force%20when%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20is%20greater%20than%20%2490%5Eo%24.%20The%20Newton-Euler%20equation%20above%20is%20a%20second-order%20nonlinear%20differential%20equation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%202.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20The%20gravitational%20term%20is%20%24r_%7Bcm%7D%5Ccos(%5Ctheta)mg%24.%20Evaluate%20%24%5Ccos%5Ctheta%24%20at%20%24%5Ctheta%20%3D%2090%5Eo%24%2C%20at%20%24%5Ctheta%20%3D%20135%5Eo%24%2C%20and%20at%20%24%5Ctheta%20%3D%20180%5Eo%24.%20At%20which%20of%20these%20knee%20angles%20does%20gravity%20resist%20the%20extension%20most%20strongly%2C%20and%20where%20does%20it%20do%20nothing%20at%20all%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20muscle%20term%20is%20%24r_M%20F_M%24.%20Two%20muscles%20could%20produce%20the%20same%20joint%20moment%20with%20very%20different%20forces.%20What%20would%20have%20to%20differ%20between%20them%3F%0A%20%20%20%203.%20The%20equation%20is%20called%20*nonlinear*.%20Point%20to%20the%20term%20that%20makes%20it%20so.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20length%20of%20the%20quadriceps%20muscle-tendon%20unit%20depends%20on%20the%20knee%20angle%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%20%3D%20L_%7BMT0%7D%20-%20r_M%20(%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Cpi%2F2)%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Look%20carefully%20at%20what%20these%20equations%20imply.%20If%20we%20excite%20the%20muscle%2C%20it%20generates%20force%3B%20that%20force%20is%20transmitted%20to%20the%20leg%20segment%20and%20accelerates%20it%3B%20the%20rotation%20changes%20the%20muscle-tendon%20length%20and%20hence%20the%20muscle%20velocity%3B%20and%20those%20in%20turn%20change%20the%20muscle%20force.%20We%20already%20saw%20in%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%20that%20muscle%20force%20is%20related%20to%20muscle%20length%20and%20velocity%20through%20a%20first-order%20ODE.%20So%20muscle%20force%20and%20joint%20angle%20are%20described%20by%20two%20*coupled*%20ODEs%2C%20and%20neither%20can%20be%20solved%20without%20the%20other.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Mathematically%2C%20the%20musculoskeletal%20system%20we%20modeled%20has%20as%20state%20variables%20%24L_M%24%2C%20%24%5Ctheta%24%2C%20and%20%24%5Comega%20%3D%20%5Cdot%7B%5Ctheta%7D%24.%20(Muscle%20activation%20%24a%24%20could%20also%20be%20a%20state%20variable%20in%20other%20situations%2C%20but%20not%20in%20this%20problem%2C%20where%20we%20hold%20it%20fixed%20as%20an%20input.)%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20rewrite%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equation%20in%20a%20clearer%20form%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%5E2%20%5Ctheta%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%5E2%7D%20%3D%20I%5E%7B-1%7D%20%5Cleft%5B%20r_M%20F_M%20%2B%20r_%7Bcm%7D%5Ccos(%5Ctheta)mg%20%5Cright%5D%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24F_M%24%20is%20determined%20once%20%24L_M%24%20is%20known%2C%20which%20according%20to%20the%20muscle%20model%20we%20used%20in%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%20is%20the%20solution%20of%20the%20following%20first-order%20ODE%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%20L_M%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20f_v%5E%7B-1%7D%5Cleft(%5Cdfrac%7BF_%7BSE%7D(L_%7BMT%7D-L_M%5Ccos%5Calpha)%2F%5Ccos%5Calpha%20-%20F_%7BPE%7D(L_M)%7D%7Ba%20f_l(L_M)%7D%5Cright)%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20and%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24F_M%20%3D%20F_%7BSE%7D(L_%7BMT%7D-L_M%5Ccos%5Calpha)%2F%5Ccos%5Calpha%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20To%20apply%20numerical%20methods%20to%20these%20coupled%20equations%2C%20we%20have%20to%20express%20them%20as%20a%20system%20of%20*first-order*%20differential%20equations%20(see%20%5BOrdinary%20differential%20equation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fordinary_differential_equation.py)).%20The%20trick%20is%20to%20promote%20the%20angular%20velocity%20%24%5Comega%24%20to%20a%20state%20variable%20of%20its%20own%2C%20which%20turns%20one%20second-order%20equation%20into%20two%20first-order%20ones%3A%0A%0A%20%20%20%20%24%5Cleft%5C%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cbegin%7Barray%7D%7Bl%20l%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%20L_M%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20f%5E%7B-1%7D_%7Bv%7D(L_M%2C%20L_%7BMT%7D(%5Ctheta))%2C%20%5Cquad%20%26%20L_M(t_0)%20%3D%20L_%7BM0%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%20%5Ctheta%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20%5Comega%2C%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Ctheta(t_0)%20%3D%20%5Ctheta_0%0A%20%20%20%20%5C%5C%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cdfrac%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%20%5Comega%7D%7B%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%7D%20%3D%20I%5E%7B-1%7D%20%5Cleft%5B%20r_M%20F_M(L_M%2C%20%5Ctheta)%20%2B%20r_%7Bcm%7D%5Ccos(%5Ctheta)mg%20%5Cright%5D%2C%20%5Cquad%20%26%20%5Comega(t_0)%20%3D%20%5Comega_0%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cend%7Barray%7D%0A%20%20%20%20%5Cright.%24%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Guiding%20questions%203.**%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20In%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%20%3D%20L_%7BMT0%7D%20-%20r_M(%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Cpi%2F2)%24%2C%20the%20sign%20in%20front%20of%20%24r_M%24%20is%20negative.%20Confirm%20that%20this%20means%20the%20quadriceps%20*shortens*%20as%20the%20knee%20extends%20(%24%5Ctheta%24%20grows%20past%20%24%5Cpi%2F2%24).%20Does%20that%20agree%20with%20the%20prediction%20you%20wrote%20for%20Challenge%200%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20The%20three%20equations%20are%20coupled.%20Find%20the%20term%20in%20the%20third%20equation%20that%20depends%20on%20the%20first%20equation's%20state%2C%20and%20the%20term%20in%20the%20first%20equation%20that%20depends%20on%20the%20second%20equation's%20state.%20That%20pair%20of%20arrows%20is%20the%20feedback%20loop.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20Why%20is%20%24%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7D%5Ctheta%2F%5Cmathrm%7Bd%7Dt%20%3D%20%5Comega%24%20not%20a%20physical%20statement%20about%20muscles%20at%20all%3F%20What%20is%20it%20doing%20in%20the%20system%3F%0A%0A%20%20%20%20**Challenge%201.**%20In%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%2C%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%24%20was%20a%20function%20you%20wrote%20by%20hand%2C%20%60lmt_eq(t%2C%20lmt0)%60%20%E2%80%94%20a%20function%20of%20*time*.%20Here%2C%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%24%20is%20a%20function%20of%20%24%5Ctheta%24%2C%20and%20%24%5Ctheta%24%20is%20a%20state%20the%20solver%20is%20computing%20as%20it%20goes.%20Explain%20in%20one%20sentence%20why%20this%20makes%20the%20problem%20qualitatively%20harder%20than%20the%20previous%20notebook%2C%20even%20though%20the%20muscle%20model%20is%20identical.%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Let's%20solve%20this%20problem%20in%20Python.%20First%2C%20let's%20import%20the%20necessary%20Python%20libraries%20and%20customize%20the%20environment%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20import%20numpy%20as%20np%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib.pyplot%20as%20plt%0A%20%20%20%20import%20matplotlib%0A%20%20%20%20from%20scipy.integrate%20import%20odeint%0A%20%20%20%20from%20scipy%20import%20interpolate%0A%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22lines.linewidth%22%5D%20%3D%202%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22font.size%22%5D%20%3D%2012%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rcParams%5B%22lines.markersize%22%5D%20%3D%204%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22axes%22%2C%20grid%3DTrue%2C%20labelsize%3D12%2C%20titlesize%3D13%2C%20ymargin%3D0.01)%0A%20%20%20%20matplotlib.rc(%22legend%22%2C%20numpoints%3D1%2C%20fontsize%3D10)%0A%20%20%20%20return%20np%2C%20odeint%2C%20plt%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20The%20muscle%20model%20itself%20is%20the%20class%20%60Thelen2003%60%2C%20the%20same%20one%20used%20in%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py).%20Instead%20of%20importing%20it%20from%20an%20external%20%60muscles.py%60%20file%2C%20we%20define%20it%20at%20the%20end%20of%20this%20notebook%2C%20so%20the%20notebook%20is%20self-contained%20and%20runs%20anywhere%2C%20including%20in%20the%20browser%20at%20%5Bmarimo.app%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmarimo.app%2F).%0A%0A%20%20%20%20Same%20for%20its%20parameters%20and%20initial%20states%2C%20which%20we%20write%20directly%20as%20Python%20dictionaries.%20These%20are%20the%20values%20from%20the%20exercise%20in%20chapter%204%20of%20Nigg%20and%20Herzog%20(2006)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell%0Adef%20_()%3A%0A%20%20%20%20parameters%20%3D%20%7B%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22id%22%3A%20%22%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22name%22%3A%20%22%22%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22u_max%22%3A%201.0%2C%20%20%23%20maximum%20value%20for%20muscle%20excitation%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22u_min%22%3A%200.01%2C%20%20%23%20minimum%20value%20for%20muscle%20excitation%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22t_act%22%3A%200.015%2C%20%20%23%20activation%20time%20constant%20%5Bs%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22t_deact%22%3A%200.050%2C%20%20%23%20deactivation%20time%20constant%20%5Bs%5D%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22lmopt%22%3A%200.093%2C%20%20%23%20optimal%20CE%20length%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22alpha0%22%3A%200.0%2C%20%20%23%20pennation%20angle%20at%20rest%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22fm0%22%3A%207400.0%2C%20%20%23%20maximum%20isometric%20muscle%20force%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22gammal%22%3A%200.45%2C%20%20%23%20CE%20force-length%20shape%20factor%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22kpe%22%3A%205.0%2C%20%20%23%20PE%20exponential%20shape%20factor%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22epsm0%22%3A%200.6%2C%20%20%23%20PE%20passive%20muscle%20strain%20due%20to%20maximum%20isometric%20force%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22vmmax%22%3A%2010.0%2C%20%20%23%20CE%20force-velocity%20maximum%20velocity%20(concentric)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%22fmlen%22%3A%201.4%2C%20%20%23%20CE%20force-velocity%20maximum%20force%20(lengthening)%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20 meter%20choices%20and%20numerical%20tolerances%20with%20each%20result.%0A%0A%20%20%20%201.%20**Activation%20level.**%20The%20helper%20functions%20fix%20%24a%20%3D%201%24.%20Change%20%60a%60%20to%20%240.5%24%20and%20then%20%240.1%24%20in%20both%20%60muscle_velocity%60%20and%20%60muscle_force%60%2C%20and%20re-run.%20Does%20the%20knee%20still%20reach%20full%20extension%3F%20Is%20the%20relationship%20between%20activation%20and%20final%20angle%20linear%3F%0A%20%20%20%202.%20**Gravity.**%20Set%20%60G%20%3D%200%60%20and%20re-run.%20How%20much%20of%20the%20movement%20was%20being%20resisted%20by%20the%20weight%20of%20the%20leg%3F%20Then%20set%20%60MASS%20%3D%2020%60%20and%20explain%20the%20result%20using%20both%20terms%20of%20the%20Newton-Euler%20equation.%0A%20%20%20%203.%20**Starting%20posture.**%20Start%20the%20simulation%20from%20a%20more%20extended%20knee%2C%20%60state0%20%3D%20%5B0.087%2C%202*np.pi%2F3%2C%200%5D%60.%20Careful%3A%20the%20initial%20muscle%20length%20is%20no%20longer%20consistent%20with%20that%20angle.%20Work%20out%20the%20correct%20%24L_%7BM0%7D%24%20from%20%24L_%7BMT%7D%20%3D%20L_%7BMT0%7D%20-%20r_M(%5Ctheta%20-%20%5Cpi%2F2)%24%2C%20assuming%20the%20tendon%20starts%20at%20slack%20length.%0A%20%20%20%204.%20**Simulation%20duration.**%20Extend%20%60time%60%20to%20%240.3%24%20s%20and%20re-run%20with%20the%20constant%20moment%20arm.%20What%20happens%2C%20and%20why%20is%20the%20result%20no%20longer%20physically%20meaningful%3F%20Relate%20your%20answer%20to%20Challenge%205.%0A%20%20%20%205.%20**A%20stronger%20muscle.**%20Double%20%60fm0%60%20in%20the%20parameters.%20Does%20the%20knee%20extend%20twice%20as%20fast%3F%20Explain%20any%20nonlinearity%20using%20the%20force-velocity%20relationship.%0A%20%20%20%206.%20**Tendon%20compliance.**%20Make%20the%20tendon%20more%20compliant%20by%20increasing%20%60epst0%60%20to%20%240.08%24.%20How%20does%20the%20extra%20tendon%20stretch%20change%20the%20fiber%20velocity%20early%20in%20the%20movement%3F%0A%20%20%20%207.%20**Moment%20arm%20sensitivity.**%20Multiply%20the%20output%20of%20%60rm_const%60%20by%20%241.5%24%20and%20re-run.%20Compare%20against%20the%20measured%2C%20angle-dependent%20moment%20arm.%20Does%20a%20uniformly%20larger%20moment%20arm%20reproduce%20the%20measured%20result%3F%20What%20does%20this%20tell%20you%20about%20the%20value%20of%20measured%20musculoskeletal%20geometry%3F%0A%20%20%20%208.%20**Adding%20an%20antagonist.**%20Sketch%20(you%20do%20not%20have%20to%20code%20it)%20how%20you%20would%20extend%20%60onelink_eq%60%20to%20include%20a%20hamstring%20acting%20as%20a%20knee%20flexor.%20What%20new%20parameters%20would%20you%20need%2C%20and%20how%20many%20state%20variables%20would%20the%20system%20have%3F%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.accordion(%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%7B'Final%20answers%20to%20original%20Problems'%3A%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%201.%20Final%20angle%20is%20not%20generally%20proportional%20to%20activation%3B%20muscle%20force%2C%20geometry%2C%20gravity%20and%20the%20chosen%20duration%20interact.%20%E2%80%9CFull%20extension%E2%80%9D%20is%20not%20a%20guaranteed%20endpoint%20of%20this%20unconstrained%20model.%0A%0A%20%20%20%202.%20Setting%20gravity%20to%20zero%20removes%20the%20gravity%20moment.%20Increasing%20mass%20changes%20the%20gravitational%20demand%3B%20a%20physically%20consistent%20mass%20change%20must%20also%20update%20%60INERTIA%60%2C%20otherwise%20the%20comparison%20isolates%20gravity%20rather%20than%20representing%20a%20heavier%20geometrically%20similar%20shank.%0A%0A%20%20%20%203.%20With%20the%20notebook%E2%80%99s%20constant%20moment%20arm%2C%20%24L_%7BM0%7D%3D0.310-0.033(2%5Cpi%2F3-%5Cpi%2F2)-0.223%3D0.0697212%24%20m%20for%20zero%20pennation%20and%20a%20slack%20tendon.%0A%0A%20%20%20%204.%20The%20unconstrained%20constant-arm%20model%20can%20pass%20the%20anatomical%20knee%20range%3B%20it%20has%20no%20joint%20stop%20or%20range-limited%20geometry.%20Extending%20time%20does%20not%20validate%20that%20extrapolation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%205.%20Doubling%20%60fm0%60%20does%20not%20generally%20double%20speed%3B%20velocity-dependent%20force%20and%20tendon%2Ffiber%20states%20change%20during%20the%20motion.%0A%0A%20%20%20%206.%20Greater%20compliance%20allows%20more%20early%20fiber%20shortening%20while%20tendon%20force%20develops%3B%20the%20exact%20transient%20depends%20on%20initial%20tendon%20stretch%20and%20activation.%0A%0A%20%20%20%207.%20A%20uniform%20multiplier%20cannot%20reproduce%20an%20arbitrary%20angle-dependent%20moment-arm%20curve.%20The%20length%20function%20must%20change%20consistently%20with%20the%20integral%20of%20that%20moment%20arm.%0A%0A%20%20%20%208.%20With%20activation%20prescribed%2C%20add%20one%20antagonist%20fiber-length%20state%3A%20four%20states%20total.%20Add%20flexor%20geometry%2C%20force%E2%80%93length%2Fvelocity%20curves%2C%20tendon%20parameters%2C%20initial%20fiber%20length%20and%20activation.%20Dynamic%20activation%20for%20both%20muscles%20adds%20two%20more%20states%2C%20for%20six%20total.%0A%20%20%20%20%22%22%22)%7D%2C%0A%20%20%20%20%20%20%20%20expanded%3DFalse%2C%0A%20%20%20%20)%0A%20%20%20%20return%0A%0A%0A%40app.cell(hide_code%3DTrue)%0Adef%20_(mo)%3A%0A%20%20%20%20mo.md(r%22%22%22%0A%20%20%20%20%23%23%20Go%20deeper%0A%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BMuscle%20modeling%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_modeling.py)%20%E2%80%94%20where%20the%20force-length%2C%20force-velocity%2C%20and%20activation%20functions%20used%20here%20were%20derived.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BMuscle%20simulation%5D(https%3A%2F%2Fmolab.marimo.io%2Fgithub%2FBMClab%2FBMC%2Fblob%2Fmaster%2Fnotebooks%2Fmuscle_simulation.py)%20%E2%80%94%20the%20same%20muscle%20model%2C%20but%20with%20the%20muscle-tendon%20length%20prescribed%20instead%20of%20produced%20by%20the%20movement.%0A%20%20%20%20-%20%5BIntroduction%20to%20numerical%20solution%20of%20Ordinary%20Differential%20Equations%5D(https%3
